requirement:
The bundled languages report each recognized source comment as `Comment` on
the item that owns it under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.
Each comment in a run has its own span and the run's owner. Consumers interpret
the comment text.
rationale:
structural: The one structural obligation in the text is that comments are reported as the `Comment` attachment kind on the owning item. That means `AttachmentKind::Comment`, with one attachment per comment carrying its own span. An implementation that reported comments as `Annotation` or `Other`, or merged a run into one span, would violate the clause. `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/contents.rs#impl[Outline]#2/fn[from_legacy]` meets it. It pushes one `OutlineAttachment` per comment onto `items[comment.owner].attachments`, with `kind: AttachmentKind::Comment` and a span built from that comment's `byte_start` and `byte_end`. The root also extends the item's span to cover the attachments and sorts them by start. The `AttachmentKind` enum in the same file defines the `Comment` variant. The text leaves comment ownership to `requirements.references.outline_comments`, which is cited as context. "Consumers interpret the comment text" places no obligation on the implementation.

behavioral: The subject has three obligations. (1) Each recognized comment in the bundled languages is reported as a `Comment` attachment. (2) That attachment is on the owner given by `requirements.references.outline_comments`. (3) Each comment in a run has its own span and the run's owner. The text says consumers interpret comment text, so that sentence adds no obligation.

Test evidence:
- **Recognition and kind:** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_classify_only_their_attachment_syntax]` checks the `Comment` kind and exact span text across the languages. The languages are Python, Rust block comments, TypeScript, TSX, CSS, YAML, TOML and Markdown HTML blocks, and the test also covers plain text. It also checks that literals, strings and inline HTML comments are not reported. Consecutive TOML comments `# first` and `# second` come back as two separate attachments with their own spans.
- **Owner assignment per language:** `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs#fn[comment_runs_follow_the_same_rules_in_every_language]` asserts owners in Python, TypeScript, TSX, CSS, TOML, YAML and Markdown. The cases cover leading runs, trailing comments on the same line, comments before the next sibling, comments at the end of a container, and top-level comments that belong to the root. The helper `comment_owner` reads the legacy outline's comments.
- **SDK mapping:** `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/contents.rs#impl[Outline]#2/fn[from_legacy]` is implemented as a plain copy. It pushes each legacy comment onto `items[comment.owner].attachments` as a `Comment` with the same byte span. The Rust SDK-level test `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[rust_attachments_keep_the_owner_kind_and_original_bytes]` checks this end to end. It asserts that the `//!` comment attaches to the root, that two `///` lines are separate attachments with non-overlapping spans on `fn f`, and that a trailing `//` comment attaches to `fn f`.

I found no obligation without a test, and no marking gap.

text: :::{req} attachments.comments
The bundled languages report each recognized source comment as `Comment` on
the item that owns it under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.
Each comment in a run has its own span and the run's owner. Consumers interpret
the comment text.
:::{req} outline_comments
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph remains ordinary paragraph text. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. Habeas MUST retain the
one-based line and UTF-8 byte column of each inline role’s opening brace or
fenced reference’s first opening colon. When siblings share a line, the
reference belongs to the item owning the comment at that position. A reference
in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
